newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso weaker on rate cut, arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso weaker on rate cut, arbitrage play.

text.p: The Philippine peso opened weaker at 26.384 and 26.385 to the dollar after the Central Bank cut its overnight rates earlier in the day, traders said.

The usual weekend arbitrage play also contributed to the peso weakness, they added. Banks usually buy dollars on Friday for settlement on Monday and earn higher interest rate offered by peso securities during the weekend.
On Wednesday, the peso closed at 26.378.
"This was expected. This is just a knee-jerk reaction to the rate cut," one trader said.

The Central Bank cut its overnight borrowing rate by one percentage point to 13.0 percent from 14.0 percent, narrowing the interest rate premium offered by peso-denominated debt securities compared to U.S. instruments.
Traders reacted by converting to dollars, but the buying was tempered when Central Bank started selling dollars at 26.385.
"This is a good move by the Central Bank. The market has somewhat calmed down," another trader said.
A total of $40 million were traded after 35 minutes of trade. -- Ramoncito dela Cruz (63 2) 841-8938 Fax 817-6267
